neighbours.label: a verb describing the posture of the eyes, lips or face in a description of expression (eyes turned up, lips curled, eyes crinkled)
fire: The old dog lay by the fire with one eye turned toward the door.
She said nothing, but her lips curled into a slow smile.
When he laughed, the corners of his eyes crinkled up.
The statue shows a bearded king with an upturned nose and narrow eyes.
Her eyes narrowed as she studied the stranger across the room.
His mouth twisted into a grin when he saw the cake.
The baby's brow furrowed and her lower lip trembled.
His eyes rimmed with tears as he read the old letter.
quiet: The old dog lay by the fire and waited for dinner to be served.
She said nothing, but she put the kettle on for tea.
When he laughed, the whole table started laughing too.
The statue shows a bearded king holding a sword and a shield.
She studied the stranger across the room for a long time.
He was happy when he saw the cake on the table.
The baby woke up and started to cry for her bottle.
He sat by the window as he read the old letter.

notes: card: ' turned' x8, rimmed, crinkled, curled into in facial descriptions
